title: Aegis Retail — Eval Workshop Agenda and Success Metrics
body:
Purpose and scope:

This doc is a working agenda for the Aegis Retail evaluation workshop and a concise acceptance rubric for the 6-week evaluation sprint. The goal: give Aegis product and infra teams a concrete plan to validate Redwood’s hosted inference integration for their in-store conversational assistant and batch product categorization pipeline, quantify cost/latency tradeoffs, and produce a recommended production deployment pattern (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

Key outcomes we will aim to deliver by the end of the workshop and sprint:
- Baseline latency and cost per query for 3 candidate models (open Llama-compat variants) on a representative Aegis traffic sample.
- Measured quality on Aegis prompt set: precision/recall proxies, answer relevance score, and misclassification rate for product categorization.
- A rollout recommendation with estimated monthly cost, latency SLOs, and fallback behavior for capacity events.
- A short list of infra/integration gaps and mitigation steps for private deployment if required.

Attendees (recommended):
- Aegis: Rachel Kim (Product), Omar Farouk (Infra), Lina Torres (Retail Ops)
- Redwood SE: Nikhil Roy (Lead), Sofia Martinez (Eval engineer), Marco Heller (Infra), Ethan Caldwell (Metrics)
- Optional: Redwood Solutions Architect on private deployments

Workshop agenda (90 minutes) — Day 1 on-site / remote hybrid:
1) 0–10 min: Introductions, success definition alignment. Quick readout of Aegis KPIs: target response latency, monthly query volume, regulation/data residency constraints.
2) 10–30 min: Data & integration walkthrough (Aegis team). What sample payloads look like, auth patterns, anonymization needs, and current in-store device connectivity.
3) 30–50 min: Redwood runtime overview & options mapping. Explain hosted, dedicated, private tradeoffs with emphasis on latency/cost. Show live perf benchmark dashboard for reference workloads.
4) 50–75 min: Hands-on narrow-scope exercise. Run three quick live queries (representative conversational, category classification, and edge-case query) against a sandbox endpoint so Aegis sees response times, token usage, and structured output capabilities.
5) 75–90 min: Define evaluation sprint plan, owners, and success metrics. Agree on data exchange methods and scheduled check-ins.

Evaluation sprint: 6-week plan (high level)
- Week 0 (prep): Dataset handoff (anonymized sample: 50k conversational turns + 25k product descriptions), credential exchange to sandbox project, create monitoring dashboards.
- Weeks 1–2 (baseline): Run baseline load tests against hosted API and collect latency and cost metrics under low/medium load. Run quality evaluation on prompt set.
- Weeks 3–4 (variants): Run identified optimizations — batching, KV-prefix caching, and a quantized model variant. Evaluate Dedicated (small pool) in parallel if Aegis requests.
- Week 5 (edge cases & long tail): Stress tests, rate-limited scenarios, and failure injection; validate graceful degradation (fallback model / simplified response).
- Week 6 (wrap & recommend): Collate metrics, produce recommendation brief, and run a short readout session with Aegis execs.

Success criteria and acceptance rubric (must be explicit):
- Latency: median end-to-end response < 350ms for conversational short-turns at 95th percentile traffic scenario, or clearly documented tradeoff if Aegis prefers higher accuracy over latency.
- Cost: hosted deployment demonstrably under $0.015 per query for average conversational payload (as measured in baseline tests), with dedicated cost estimates showing at least 20% lower unit cost at committed volumes.
- Quality: Answer relevance score >= 0.85 on Aegis’ 1,200 prompt evaluation set (human-reviewed scoring rubric), and product categorization F1 >= 0.92 on labeled sample.
- Reliability: System recovers automatically from a simulated GPU node failure within 90s and preserves in-flight prefix caches when possible (or documents the cache window loss and impact).
- Integration: Auth and data flow validated end-to-end (sandbox) with no PII in logs; KMS integration tested for private option during week 2 if requested.
- Observability: Per-route latency and token-cost dashboards created and accessible to Aegis; alerting threshold (e.g., p95 latency breach) configured and tested.

Acceptance tests (concrete checks we will run):
- Scripted run: 5k synthetic conversational queries at ramp to target QPS; assert p50/p95/p99 against targets and collect per-token cost.
- Hand-eval: 300 randomly selected responses scored by Aegis product team for relevance/accuracy.
- Categorization eval: Run labeled 10k test set, compute precision/recall/F1 and confusion matrix.
- Failure sim: Kill one inference worker and validate fallback policy and time-to-recover metrics.

Infra & security checklist (quick):
- VPN / IP allowlist for sandbox endpoints — owner: Aegis infra (Omar).
- Credential rotation policy and temporary service accounts — owner: Redwood SE (Marco).
- Ensure logs scrub PII before sending to Redwood-hosted observability (if chosen).
- KMS integration plan if private required — escalate to Redwood security for review in week 2.

Open questions & risks to resolve during workshop:
- Does Aegis require on-prem inference for any region due to data residency? If yes, we need a private-deployment trial path.
- Expected QPS distribution by store/location (bursty vs steady) — impacts batching and caching strategy.
- Will edge devices operate offline and batch-forward logs later? If yes, offline-first sync semantics to be defined.

Deliverables at sprint close:
- 1-page recommendation memo (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with cost/latency tables.
- Dashboard link and raw measurement CSVs.
- Mini-playbook for rollout (canary steps, throttles, rollback criteria).
- A short recording of the readout and a prioritized backlog of follow-up items.

Immediate next steps (before workshop):
1) Aegis to share anonymized sample dataset (dropbox/gs link) and traffic shape notes by 2025-11-24.
2) Redwood to provision sandbox project and share credentials (by 2025-11-26).
3) Prior to workshop, Redwood will prepare 3 candidate model config files and a short benchmark run to demo (Sofia).
4) Confirm participants and calendar invite (Nikhil).

Notes to SEs (internal):
- Keep the live demo tightly scoped — pick 3 examples that highlight structured output, short-latency conversational turn, and the failure case (long context).
- Instrument the sandbox with token-level cost estimation so Aegis sees dollar impact in real-time.
- Flag any model licensing concerns early; prefer open models with permissive terms for an easy trial.

Contact points:
